items.title: Onaje Allan Gumbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001
items.q: that’s what Cannonball did, Duke did, Louis Armstrong did, Barry Harris does. Okay? There are a lot of musicians who do talk. Frank Foster does, okay.

ctx.x: Yeah. I mean I heard a concert where Buster Williams was playing. And he has this incredible piece called “Christina.” It’s one of the most beautiful ballads you ever want to hear. But he was a side man in this one group. They did it. You didn’t know the name of the song, let alone know that Buster wrote it. And I think in a room full of people it might be nice to know that it wasn’t written by a piano player, it wasn’t written by a horn player, but this beautifully harmonically intricate song was written by the…

he’s a great composer at the same time. And this bothers me in the music. The lack of concern for the audience. And you don’t have to become shuckin’ and jivin’ all kinds of stuff, but just engage, to communicate. I remember Stephon Harris who is one of the brightest young vibraphonist musicians out there. I remember going to his gig. And he was getting ready to announce the song and he couldn’t remember the tune. And he played it up. He had everybody cracking up.
